narrative: Material PL2__M4F36DB1 exhibits an erratic demand regime (CV=0.58) with a strong confirmed upward trend of 127% over the observation window, driven primarily by a volume surge from January 2026 onward. Lead times are unstable (CV=0.42, mean 2.61 days), compounding replenishment uncertainty and requiring a meaningful safety buffer. The current SAP safety stock of 2,574 units is insufficient at the 95% service level; the statistically derived requirement is 6,651 units. An (r,Q) continuous-review policy with EOQ-sized batches of 20,648 units reduces annual ordering frequency and cuts total inventory costs by approximately 90% while remaining within storage capacity limits.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Given non-zero demand on ~98% of working days and a high but continuous demand pattern, a continuous-review (r,Q) policy is appropriate. EOQ batch sizing minimises the sum of ordering and holding costs under the observed annual demand rate. The MOQ of 792 units is well below the EOQ of 20,648, so the economic quantity governs without MOQ binding.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity of 73,428 units is not binding (safety_stock + order_quantity = 27,299 units). However, if the upward demand trend continues, the safety stock will need to be revised upward, potentially approaching capacity within 12-18 months if demand doubles again.
research_insights.escalation_flag: Demand trend of +127% is a critical escalation signal. The current SAP policy is structurally misaligned with actual demand; immediate policy update and root-cause investigation of the Jan 2026 demand surge are required.
